exposure: COVID-19 emergency contingency and response plans
outcome: maternal, newborn, and child health service coverage (antenatal care, postnatal care, child routine vaccination, care-seeking for sick children)
cohort: Households (3375 in the first survey) in two provinces (one rural, one urban) of Burkina Faso, focusing on maternal, newborn, and child health service utilization.
finding: The COVID-19 pandemic did not cause major reversals in the coverage of most maternal, newborn, and child health services in Burkina Faso, but it did lead to a dramatic drop in caesarean-section deliveries in urban areas.
mod_finding: The number of caesarean-section deliveries in urban areas dramatically dropped during the pandemic, potentially due to health staff shortages, facility congestion, fear of COVID-19, and prioritization of emergency cases.
cross-section timing: February to March 2020 (pre-pandemic) and May to June 2022 (two years after pandemic onset)
